title: Viewer: a pick of a part only Code draws lays out all of Code first (13.7 s for ask.digest)
description:
On docair's own page (1440x960), the word digest's popup offers 'see ask.digest'. Clicking it takes 13.7 s before the camera arrives. docair-ai.ask.digest is a function. Only the Code layer draws it as a part of its own, so select() runs layerFor(), which picks Code, then showLayer('code') lays out all of Code: 385 parts and 631 lines.

Measured with headless Chromium on a page scanned 2026-11-18 (1188 nodes, 1591 edges):

| What | Time |
|---|---|
| pick ask.digest from Network or Apps (layer switch to Code) | 13.7 s |
| pick ask.digest again, already at Code | 0.45 s (camera only) |
| Apps with docair-ai.ask opened (drill) | 0.56 s, draws ask.digest |
| layerFor() itself | 1 ms |

Which box holds ask.digest at each layer: Overview: docair-lib. Apps: docair-ai. Infra, Network, Kubernetes: none.

Cause: SPEC §3.4 says a pick of a part the layer leaves out goes to the first layer that is about it. For a function, that layer is always Code, and Code is the most expensive layout on the page (docair-4wk.22).

How to tackle: open the boxes that hold the part on the layer the reader is on, as drill() does. When this layer draws no box that holds it, open them on Apps, which Code goes up to. Go to Code only when nothing else can show the part, or when the reader asks for it (a 'show it at Code' link in the details).
design: To decide in the step: which layer comes first when the current one has no box for the part (Apps, or the layer layerFor picks with its boxes opened). Whether a part that a box opened at Apps now shows keeps the breadcrumb (Apps › docair-ai › ask) so the reader can close it again. SPEC §3.4 'Selecting a part that the layer leaves out' changes with it.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's page at 1440x960, picking docair-ai.ask.digest from the word digest's popup, the tree or a link, starting at Apps or Network, shows the part readable in 1.5 s or less. The camera still frames it as SPEC §3.5 says. SPEC §3.4 says what a pick does when the layer leaves the part out. An e2e test picks a function from Apps and checks the layer, the opened box and the time.
notes: Built 2026-11-18. crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js: select() asks pickWay (@id docair-viewer.pick-way) how to show a part the picture leaves out or draws only as a closed box. It opens the part's own box on the current layer when the layer draws a box around it, else on Apps, else it goes to layerFor() as before. showWay() opens the box (unfolding folded boxes around it), sets the breadcrumb focus, and toasts 'Apps · inside ask'. enterLayer() is the reset showLayer() did. The old Code-only quiet-part branch is folded into this. Correction to the description: at Apps the old pick selected the closed box docair-ai (2 ms) and never showed the function; only Network, Infra and Kubernetes went to Code. Numbers on docair's page (1440x960): ask.digest at Network 14.1 s -> 0.57 s drawn, 1.0 s with the camera (Apps, docair-ai.ask opened); at Apps -> 0.06 s drawn, 0.48 s with the camera, zoom x sc 1.0. A Deployment picked at Infra opens its release box there (0.5 s). docs/SPEC.md §3.4: new paragraph and a before/now table. e2e/tests/layout.spec.ts (e2e.layout): 'a function picked at Apps comes with its box opened, details first' and 'a function the layer has no box for comes at Apps' (Infra -> Apps for the cart's function, Infra keeps the cluster's service, a closed box at Code opens there). Time is measured by script on docair's page, not in e2e (the fixtures are small).
close_reason: A pick of a part the layer leaves out, or draws only inside a closed box, opens the part's box on the current layer or on Apps, and goes to the layer about the part only when neither can show it. On docair's page, ask.digest picked at Network comes in 1.0 s instead of 14.1 s. SPEC §3.4 and e2e.layout cover it; e2e 59/59 pass.

title: Uploads: run no indexer, read no code index outside the upload
description: Reported by the viewer session while reading docair-server: run_scan scans an upload with the upload's own docair.toml. (1) [code] run_indexers = true made the server run rust-analyzer scip on the uploaded Cargo project when rust-analyzer is installed (local server, e2e): rust-analyzer runs build scripts and proc macros, so an upload could run code on the server. Confirmed by hand: an upload whose build.rs writes a file did write it. (2) [code] scip paths were joined to the root unchecked: ../.., an absolute path or /dev/zero made the server read or hang on files outside the upload.
acceptance_criteria: An upload with run_indexers = true and a build.rs runs nothing; scip paths outside the root, absolute, through a link or to a device are W113; the local CLI still runs rust-analyzer on the user's own code.
notes: Built: Options::untrusted (docair-core lib.rs): scan sets [code] run_indexers = false for it; docair-server run_scan passes untrusted: true; CLI callers use ..Options::default(). docair-core config::inside(root, rel): relative, canonicalized (links resolved) and still under the root, a regular file or folder; docair-lang-rust index_of reads scip only through it, else W113 'the code index X is no file inside the project'. Tests: docair-core config inside_tests::a_path_in_docair_toml_stays_inside_the_root; docair-server an_upload_runs_no_code_and_reads_nothing_outside (fails with 'the upload's build script ran' when untrusted is off). title: Upload: the page looks frozen while it uploads, scans and draws (stuck at 'Generating… 0%')
description: Uploading docair's own folder (286 files, 7.8 MB) to a local docair-server: the button shows 'Generating… 0%' for 8 s, then the result view appears with an empty frame for another 1.5 s while the viewer lays out its first layer. Nothing moves and nothing says what is happening. Causes: (1) Angular 22's provideHttpClient() uses fetch by default, and fetch reports no upload progress. app.config.ts says XHR, but withXhr() is missing, so the percentage never moves. (2) Nothing is shown while the server scans or while the response downloads. (3) The generated page tells its parent nothing until it is ready, and the viewer shows nothing while a long layout runs: about 1.5 s for docair's first layer, up to 11 s at Code. How to tackle: withXhr(). One progress line with a bar for each phase: reading the folder (drag and drop), uploading (percent, MB), docair reads the files (indeterminate, elapsed seconds), receiving the page (percent). The viewer posts docair:ready to the parent, and the result view covers the frame with 'Drawing the page…' until then. The viewer itself shows 'Drawing…' and yields a frame before a layout that is likely to take long.
acceptance_criteria: Uploading a folder shows each phase with its progress: percent and MB while uploading, elapsed seconds while docair reads the files, percent while the page arrives, and 'Drawing the page…' until the page is ready. Regenerating shows the same. An e2e test checks the phases with a delayed scan answer.
notes: Built. Web app (web/src/app): app.config.ts uses provideHttpClient(withXhr()); Angular 22's default is fetch, which reports no upload progress, so the old percentage never moved. New progress-line component (@id docair-web.progress): the step 'N of 4', a bar (filled for upload and download, moving for scan and draw), bytes and percent, seconds while waiting, and after 10 s 'big projects take a while'. app.ts tracks the phases from HttpEvents: upload (UploadProgress), scan (all bytes sent), download (ResponseHeader, DownloadProgress), then the result. The upload panel shows the line under Generate, plus 'Reading the folder · N files so far' while a dropped folder is walked. The result view shows the compact line in its bar while regenerating, and covers the frame with 'Drawing the page: <layer> · N parts, M lines · s' until the page posts docair:ready (30 s fallback after load). Viewer: renderNow says what it draws (drawing(), @id docair-viewer.drawing), posts docair:drawing to the parent and yields a paint first (nextPaint, with a 60 ms fallback for hidden pages). A note with a spinner shows in the middle of the canvas once a layout takes 250 ms (CSS delay; compositor-run, so it moves while the layout holds the thread). Inside the web app it is left to the app until ready. Boot posts docair:ready, or failed: true. Measured on docair's folder (286 files, 7.8 MB) at about 3 MB/s, throttled: upload 2.7 s with a moving percentage, server 0.3 s, page 5.7 MB in 2 s, drawing 1.4 s; before, it sat at 'Generating… 0%' throughout. The 8 s server wait seen before was rust-analyzer running on the upload, fixed by the adapters epic (docair-4wk.23). Tests: e2e generate.spec.ts 'each step of a generation shows how far it is' (shop plus a 600 kB note, CDP throttling, phases upload/scan/download/draw in order with their texts); levels.spec.ts 'the page says what it draws while it lays out'. e2e 55/55; docair check 0/0. Docs: SPEC §1 (viewer note) and new §1.3, web/README.md, docs/meanings.toml [progress].
close_reason: Every step of a generation now says where it is: upload percent and MB, docair's reading in seconds, the page coming back, and the page drawing itself until it is ready.

title: Viewer: lay out off the main thread; the page freezes for a long layout
description:
The viewer inlines elk.bundled.js, which runs ELK in a fake worker on the main thread. docair's router (gridLines) runs there too. While Code lays out on docair's page (13.7 s at 1440x960), the page paints 47 frames, and the longest gap is 1.6 s. Hovering, panning, scrolling and the layer buttons wait until the layout is done.

Where the time goes (CPU profile of one Code layout):

| Part | Time |
|---|---|
| ELK, 24 calls over 6 placements (2 directions + 4 TOPDOWN_WAYS) | 7.5 s, longest call 1.6 s |
| gridLines (search 4.0 s, roughWay 1.6 s) | 5.7 s |
| everything else (Cytoscape, labels, boxes) | under 0.5 s |

How to tackle: run ELK in a real Worker, made from a Blob of the inlined ELK worker script (elkjs takes workerUrl or workerFactory). Move gridLines into the same worker if its inputs can be passed as plain data. Check that it works from file://, inside the web app's iframe, and under the page's CSP (worker-src). A newer layout run can then terminate the older one instead of waiting for it.
acceptance_criteria: During a Code layout on docair's page, no frame gap is longer than 100 ms, and a click on another layer stops the layout and draws that layer. The page works the same from file://, from docair serve and inside the web app. Layout results are the same as on the main thread (the layer script's crossings and detours do not change).
notes: Built 2026-11-18. viewer.html: the ELK and viewer script tags have ids (docair-elk, docair-app). viewer.js: the layout worker (@id docair-viewer.layout-worker) is a Blob of the ELK source plus the viewer source, wrapped in a function so 'use strict' holds. In the worker the script only calls serveLayouts() (no boot). That takes self.onmessage back from ELK's own worker code, and ELK runs there with its fake worker. computeLayout() is the old layoutFor body, made pure: flow hints go across as data (hintsData/hintsFrom), and fitZoom/topdownFirst/topdownPlace read the canvas size and direction from a ctx argument instead of S. measure() uses an OffscreenCanvas in the worker. layoutJob() shares the job under way for the same key. A newer picture terminates the worker (stopLayout) and the next job starts a fresh one. If the worker fails to start or breaks, workerFailed() lays out on the page from then on, the job under way too. firstLayer() uses the worker as well, and stops when the reader picks a layer first. The drag reroute stays on the page. Numbers on docair's page (1440x960, 1977 edges): during the 23 s Code layout the longest frame gap is 20 ms with no long tasks (was a 6.1 s task, gaps up to 1.6 s). Clicking Apps 1.5 s into a Code layout draws Apps 0.78 s later. Worker vs page on the same picture: network 493/499 ms, apps 603/650, k8s 567/609, code 23.1/23.6 s, and identical positions and routes on all four. Works from file://, over plain HTTP, and in a srcdoc iframe with the web app's sandbox (Chromium). e2e.layout 'the worker lays out inside the web app too'. The drawing note and the docair:drawing and docair:ready messages are unchanged. SPEC §1 and §3.5 'Beside the page, and once'.

title: Viewer: a part picked from a link must come close enough to read, and stand out
description:
Picking a part from outside the canvas selects it and moves the camera to it. Afterwards the part is often too small to read and too faint to spot: the reader cannot tell at a glance which box it is, or where in the picture it sits.

Where a pick comes from (each calls select(id, true) in crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js):

| From | Function |
|------|----------|
| a part's name in the details | nodeLink |
| a row in the tree | renderTree |
| a diagnostic | renderDiagButton |
| a chip in a walk's step card | stepCard |
| "Read more" and "Show it" in a word's popup; a part named in an explanation | termMore, wireTerms |
| `#id` in the page's URL | the page's start |

Why (select, @id docair-viewer.show-details): the camera centres on the part at zoom max(current zoom, 1).

- It ignores how small the part is drawn. The layout draws what is inside a box smaller (node data `sc`, font size `fs`), so at zoom 1 a function inside a module inside a program has a few pixels of text.
- It does not fit the part: a large box at zoom 1 can run off the canvas.
- The mark is weak: a selected node gets a 3 px accent border, the same as a search hit (node.hit). Nothing draws the eye once the camera stops.
- A part on another layer, or in a closed box, is laid out again first (showLayer, render); the camera then starts from wherever the new layout put it.

The walk camera already solves the readable part: cameraFor and frameStep take `sc` into account, and never frame a step below zoom 0.8 in drawn size (SPEC §10.4, "never smaller than readable").

A click on the canvas itself does not move the camera, and should stay so.
design:
To decide in the step:

- Frame the picked part with cameraFor: the whole part on the canvas, its label readable (zoom × sc ≥ TOUR_MIN_ZOOM), and room around it, so its box and neighbours show where it is.
- Mark it: for example a short pulse or halo once the camera arrives, and a selected style that differs from a search hit.
- Maybe say where it is in words too: the boxes around it, as the zoom-in breadcrumb does (Apps › docair-lib › docair-core).
acceptance_criteria: After a pick from a link, the tree, a diagnostic, a step chip, a word's popup or the URL: the part is fully on the canvas, its label is readable (zoom × its draw scale ≥ 0.8, as for a walk's step), and the box around it is in view when that still fits at a readable zoom. The picked part stands out at a glance, and looks different from a search hit. A click on the canvas still does not move the camera. An e2e test picks a nested part by a link and checks the zoom and that the part is on screen. SPEC §3.4 or §3.5 says what a pick does to the camera.
notes:
Built 2026-11-18:
- crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js. The viewer session owns this file and applied the change as a patch. select() calls showPicked when a part is picked outside the canvas. New, next to cameraFor: showPicked (@id docair-viewer.show-picked), pickCamera and pulse. The camera puts the part in the middle at zoom × sc = 1, never below 0.8. The part's box stays in view when it fits at a readable zoom. A part too large to read whole is shown whole. A reader who is closer already keeps their zoom. node:selected has a halo (underlay in --accent, opacity 0.3, padding 8 × sc). It swells twice when the camera stops, except with reduced motion. .dim, .flow-dim and .carry-dim skip the selected part.
- docs/SPEC.md §3.5: new paragraph "Pick a part", with a before/now table.
- e2e/tests/pick.spec.ts (e2e.pick, 2 tests). First: a part picked by a link ends in the middle, readable, fully on the canvas, not dimmed by the search, with a halo that a search hit lacks. Second: a click on the canvas does not move the camera. The first test fails on the old viewer, where the search dimmed the picked part to 0.16.

Numbers on docair's own page (canvas 830 × 870):
| Picked | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| docair-core.build at Code | zoom × sc 0.49, words 5.9 px | 1.0, words 12 px |
| docair-server at Code | zoom 1, a box 1381 px wide, off the canvas | zoom 0.51, all in view |
| docair-server.scan_upload at Network | 0.84 | 0.85, its release box in view |

Validation: e2e 53/53 passed (results.json); docair check . has 0 errors and 0 warnings.
close_reason: A pick from a link, the tree, a diagnostic, a step chip, a word's popup or #id brings the part to the middle at its designed size (zoom × scale 1, never below 0.8), keeps its box in view when that fits, and shows a too-large part whole. A halo that pulses twice marks it, and the search, walks and data never dim it. A canvas click leaves the camera alone. Covered by e2e/tests/pick.spec.ts (passing) and SPEC §3.5.

title: Following data: the walk misses data that travels back as a reply (5 of 8 data items reach none of their lines)
description:
SPEC §3.6: Follow walks where a datum is made, then every line that carries it, in the order it travels, and those lines stay lit. On docair's own page this fails for most data. Following ◇ digest gives one step ('ask.digest makes digest') and leaves out the one line that carries it (docair-ai.ask.ask -> docair-ai.client.chat). Of the 8 data items with lines, 5 reach none of them (page 0 of 6, digest 0/1, reply 0/16, walkthrough 0/4, patch 0/5) and 3 reach some (question 7/12, files 15/18, graph 7/36).
Cause: dataTour() in crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js only walks along the arrows from the part that makes the datum. A call line carries its payload along the arrow and its reply against it, and a function that makes a datum usually returns it to its caller (ask.digest returns the digest to ask.ask, which sends it on to the model). Neither a reply nor that return is followed.
How to tackle: (1) Know which side of a line carries the datum: the payload (along the arrow) or the reply (back). The core already finds carries by matching payload and reply words (edge.carries); have it record the side (for example carries and carries_back), or let the viewer match the datum's words against payload and reply. (2) In dataTour, let the datum travel back along a line that carries it in its reply, and from its maker back to the callers of the maker. (3) Lines that carry it but that the walk cannot reach still go into the walk, at the end, so none is left out silently.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's page, following each data item walks every line that carries it, or the walk says which it could not place. Following digest walks ask.digest, then ask.ask -> client.chat. An e2e test follows a datum that a function makes and returns.
notes:
Built (viewer): dataTour in crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js walks a datum both ways. It goes on along a line whose carries name it and back along a call whose carries_back name it; a call named both ways is walked there and later back, never back then there. Where no named line goes on, it bridges inside other lines (on, back, or back then on; at most 6 lines); only a part that made the datum or got it back as an answer hands it back to its callers. A line the walk cannot reach starts its own stretch, and that step says 'Not reached from where X is made'. Data walks get one message per step (walkMessages(steps, datum), no call stack). carriedBy(e) is used for the Data list counts, the lit lines and the datum's 'Carried by' list (answer-only lines marked 'answer'); the edge tip says 'brings back'. Core side (Edge.carries_back) by the adapters epic. Tests: e2e/tests/data.spec.ts: the shop order walk now has 4 steps (create_order answers Cart); new test 'data that a function makes and returns is followed back to its caller, and on' on e2e/fixtures/answer. Numbers on docair's page (1162 nodes, 1552 edges): every walk takes every carrying line: question 18/18, files 24/24, graph 54/54, page 8/8, digest 1/1 in 3 steps (ask.digest makes, answers ask.ask, ask.ask calls chat), reply 23/23, walkthrough 6/6, patch 7/7; a walk is computed in at most 8 ms. e2e 51/51; docair check 0 errors, 0 warnings. Docs: SPEC §3.6, docs/DATA.md.
Earlier note, restored (it was replaced by mistake): Core side (from the adapters session, 2026-11-17): option (1) is a small additive change in crates/docair-core/src/resolve.rs find_carried_data. Today it matches a datum's words against the edge's payload and reply together and records edge.carries. It can record the reply-side matches separately, e.g. Edge.carries_back: Vec<String> (serde default + skip if empty, so graphs and goldens without such lines stay byte-identical). Ready to do it when this issue is scheduled; tell docair-4wk's session.
close_reason: Data walks follow a datum there and back and reach every line that carries it on docair's page; e2e covers a datum made, returned and sent on.

title: Following data: the walk plays on Apps, where its parts and lines sit inside one box
description:
Every data walk on docair's page plays at the Apps layer. A datum mostly travels between functions inside one crate, which Apps draws as one closed box: following ◇ digest marks the whole docair-ai box as the step, and the line that carries the digest is not drawn at all, because both its ends are inside that box. The reader has to find 'Open ▸ this step inside docair-ai' to see anything.
How to tackle: choose a data walk's layer by where its lines are drawn as lines: count, per layer, the carrying lines drawn between two parts against those folded into one box, so a datum that moves inside one crate plays at Code. Or keep the layer and open the boxes its steps are in, as walks already open modules at Code (walkView). Do this after the reply fix (docair-nkm), which gives the walk the lines to count.
acceptance_criteria: Following digest, reply, walkthrough or patch on docair's page shows the parts and the lit carrying lines without opening anything by hand.
notes: Built (viewer, crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js): dataLayer(base) picks a datum's layer: the one that draws most of the walk's lines as lines between two parts, not folded into one box; on a tie, fewer steps that only Open shows, then the higher layer. defaultLayer uses it for data walks; openStep gives an opened data step the datum's messages. Second cause, fixed: classify's leaf rule closed docair-ai at Code, because its direct parts (modules) are only found in the code, while the functions inside them have doc blocks. A box now stands closed only when nothing inside it has a doc block ('told' set). On docair's page (1552 edges), every data walk plays at Code with 0 steps that need Open: digest 3 steps, 2/2 lines drawn; reply 32 steps, 33/33; walkthrough 10, 9/9; patch 8, 7/12 (the rest are network hops Code leaves out). At Apps before: reply 11/33 lines drawn with 14 of 17 steps hidden in a box, patch 2/12, question 4/23. The fold fix adds 31 parts and 41 lines at Code. e2e 53/53 (data.spec covers the walks at Code); docair check 0/0. SPEC §3.4 Code row (fold rule), §10 walk layer (data walks). Cost: the first step of a data walk at Code waits for the Code layout: reply 5.7 s, patch 3.6 s, question 5.3 s on docair's page. Filed as docair-4wk.22.
close_reason: Data walks play at the layer that draws their lines; on docair's page digest, reply, walkthrough and patch show their parts and lit lines without opening a box.

title: Meanings: the page explains every word from what the project defines, code first
description:
Looking at facts on docair's page, it was not clear what a fact is, although the project defines it: the module doc of crates/docair-core/src/facts.rs ('Facts: what adapters learn from the code. Adapters report facts and never touch the graph...'), docs/ADAPTERS.md §4, docs/IMPORTS.md §2. The viewer explains only GLOSSARY.md terms (SPEC §13.2), so nothing else docair knows reaches the reader. Even the glossary's own 'adapter' entry says 'reports facts' and leaves the word unexplained.

Goal: every word a reader may not know is explained on the page, from the best source the project has, and deciding what a word means is done once and kept.

Sources docair already reads that define words:
1. Doc blocks and native docs (//!, ///; docair-4wk.4) of the symbol that implements a word: docair-core.facts, Symbol ('Something that exists in the code'), Evidence, Inferred, Draw.
2. Doc headings that name a concept ('## 4. Facts: the contract between adapters and core').
3. GLOSSARY.md entries, the place for words with no code of their own (Ingress, Helm, Terraform).

The design doc is docs/MEANINGS.md (step 1); SPEC §13 follows it.
design:
Decisions (2026-11-17):
• Source code is the best source, always. A word's definition comes first from the doc block or native doc of the symbol that implements it, then from GLOSSARY.md, then from doc headings (docs/MEANINGS.md §2).
• The glossary is checked against the code. Where an entry contradicts the code's definition, the code wins and the contradiction is reported.
• The AI may expand a definition or word it better, starting from the code's.
• Where a word is not clear (a term or an ordinary word; which of two definitions applies; whether a summary defines the word or only names a node), the AI decides. Each decision is recorded in the repository, so it is a one-off effort per word: the next run does not ask again.
• docair check warns about a word the texts use but nothing defines and no decision covers.
• docair glossary and '✦ Explain the terms' build entries from the definitions the project already has, code first, instead of writing new ones from nothing.
• The hover says where an explanation comes from (the node, the doc section, the glossary); Read more opens it.

Open for docs/MEANINGS.md:
• Where and in what format decisions are recorded: in GLOSSARY.md itself (an entry whose See: names the code, a list of words that are not terms) or in a file of their own.
• How a changed source reopens a decision (a digest of the defining text).
• How a contradiction is found (the AI, since it is about meaning), how it is kept, and how check and the page show it.
• How common node names (check, build, scan, merge) are kept from underlining every text.
• The new warning codes.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's own page, hovering 'facts' shows what a fact is from facts.rs, names the source, and Read more opens it. A second explain run on an unchanged tree asks the AI nothing new. docair check warns about an undefined word on a fixture and stays at 0 errors, 0 warnings on docair. SPEC §13 says where the page's explanations come from.

title: Import 4: AsyncAPI
description:
AsyncAPI 2.6 and 3.x.

- Channels are declared Topic meets: in 2.x the channel key, in 3.x its address (the key when there is none).
- 3.x action send and 2.x subscribe: the application sends. 3.x receive and 2.x publish: it receives. 2.x names the verbs from the other side on purpose.
- What travels: the message name, else its title, else the payload's $ref name.
- Lines from the description yield to the same relation from code inside the service; code relations without payload take the message name (evidence: the description).
- Warnings like Import 3: the description sends what no code emits; the code emits what the description doesn't list.

notes: Done 2026-11-17. docair-lang-apis: each AsyncAPI send/receive is also a Relation (emits/consumes topic:<address> (Message)) from the description symbol, so merge draws the description's lines. Core declare.rs: blocks() makes each declared channel a discovered topic node 'topic:<address>' at the system level (the id @emits topic:… resolves to), with the channel's text and a described tag 'topic:x (Message)'; settle() lets a description's line yield to the same line from code inside its service, W114 when it sends/receives what no code there does (only if that service has event lines at all), W115 when code in a service with an AsyncAPI description sends/receives a topic none declares; a description whose lines all yielded goes. word_and_prune(): emit/consume lines without a payload take the topic's message, with from_api. Fixture: api/asyncapi.yaml is fully covered by code and goes; mailer/asyncapi.yaml keeps its order.cancelled line (W114). 2.6 and 3.0 parse alike (unit test in docair-lang-apis).

title: Imports: OpenAPI and AsyncAPI descriptions
design:
- Adapter crate docair-lang-apis, registered in docair_adapters::all() (ADAPTERS.md §5.1, §5.3).

Requests that meet it take payload and reply from it when their block says nothing. Unserved operations become endpoint nodes inside the description's node, which goes into the package or service that owns its directory and disappears when nothing is left in it.
- YAML and JSON with line numbers: serde-saphyr if it gives spans (LIBRARIES.md chose it for the rules), else saphyr 0.3.3 (checked: YAML and JSON, a line per key and per parse error).

title: Import decisions: declared routes in the facts model, and five more
description:
Decisions before Import 1.

1. How facts say "this description declares a route" without serving it. Otherwise a handler plus its description are two servers of one route. Options: (a) a role on Serve: implements | describes; (b) a new fact Declare { at: Meet, payload, reply, name, evidence }. Recommended: (b), so Serve keeps meaning "this code runs here". It touches the facts model docair-4wk.2 is building now.
2. A description is its own node (kind `api`) inside its service, removed when everything in it merged. Recommended: yes.
3. Operations without a handler are drawn as endpoints (plus a warning). Recommended: yes.
4. Inside an external part, only the operations the code calls are kept, so a vendored description with hundreds of operations stays small. Recommended: yes.
5. YAML crate: serde-saphyr if it gives line numbers, else saphyr 0.3.3.
6. Dogfooding: a hand-written crates/docair-server/openapi.yaml, checked against the routes from code. Recommended: yes.
acceptance_criteria: Each choice recorded in this issue's notes; the facts-model change agreed with docair-4wk.2.
notes:
From docair-4wk.2, 2026-11-17: agreed on decision 1 (b), a separate Declare fact; Serve keeps meaning 'this code runs here'. Serve now has at: Meet (Meet::Http only so far), so Declare { by, at: Meet, payload, reply, name, evidence } fits beside it. docair-58a adds Declare, Meet::Topic and the api kind in crates/docair-core/src/facts.rs; merge ignores declares until docair-58a.3.
Decided 2026-11-17 (the user asked to implement the epic with the recommended choices): 1 (b) a separate Declare fact, agreed with docair-4wk.2. 2 yes, the description is its own node, kind api, removed when nothing is left in it. 3 yes, operations without a handler are drawn as endpoints. 4 yes, inside an external part only the operations the code calls are kept. 5 serde-saphyr =2.0.0 in [workspace.dependencies]: Spanned gives line numbers for keys and values in YAML and JSON (checked); ast-grep-config 0.51.3 needs ^2.0.0, so the pin keeps the tree on one version older than two weeks. 6 yes, crates/docair-server/openapi.yaml in Import 5.

title: Import 1: read API description files into facts
description:
New crate docair-lang-apis (LanguageAdapter), registered in docair-adapters.

- Finds descriptions: YAML by its first key (openapi, swagger, asyncapi), sniffed without parsing, so Helm templates are never parsed; JSON by name, via [import] apis (defaults **/*openapi*.json, **/*swagger*.json, **/*asyncapi*.json) and a json row in the language registry with no comment syntax, so package-lock.json and the like stay unread.
- Emits the description symbol and one declared Http meet per operation: method; base + path; payload (the body's $ref name, Order[] for arrays, else the parameter names); reply (the first 2xx schema); operationId; evidence file:line.
- Base path: the path of servers[0].url ({var} defaults, relative URLs, none = /); path-level and operation-level servers override it; 2.0 basePath; [[import.api]] base wins.
- Versions 2.0, 3.0, 3.1; 3.2 like 3.1 without the query method and additionalOperations.
- A file that can't be parsed gets the parse-failure diagnostic (ADAPTERS.md §9.4); the scan goes on.
design:
docair.toml:

[import]
apis = ["contracts/*.json"]     # more JSON files to read, besides the defaults

[[import.api]]
file    = "api/openapi.yaml"
part_of = "orders-api"          # the service it describes
base    = "/api"                # instead of the servers' path
ignore  = ["GET /healthz"]      # routes left out on purpose
acceptance_criteria: Facts tests (expected facts as sorted lines, like ADAPTERS.md §9.1) for 2.0, 3.0 and 3.1 in YAML and JSON; a broken file is reported and the scan goes on; a Helm template next to a description is untouched; the golden graphs of docair, shop and platform are unchanged (the core does not use the new facts yet).
notes: Done 2026-11-17. New crate crates/docair-lang-apis (tree.rs: YAML/JSON as a tree of nodes with lines via serde-saphyr Spanned; openapi.rs: 2.0, 3.0, 3.1, 3.2 without query/additionalOperations; asyncapi.rs: 2.x, 3.x), registered in docair-adapters before GenericAdapter. Core: facts.rs Declare/Role/Meet::Topic and Facts.declares; check.rs kind api; lang.rs json row (Family::Data); discover.rs reads JSON only when named like a description or listed; config.rs [import] apis and [[import.api]] file/part_of/base/ignore; adapter.rs Project.config. W113 = a description that cannot be read, or a part of it that is not read. Tests: 12 unit tests, crates/docair-lang-apis/tests/declares.rs (the fixture's declarations as sorted lines), golden crates/docair-adapters/tests/golden/apis.graph.json, shop and platform goldens unchanged, docair check . clean.

title: Import 2: descriptions meet the code
description:
Core: declared meets meet the code.

- A declared Http meet is matched with the code's Serve at the same meet (the path algebra from docair-4wk.6; parameter names ignored; base path optional). The serving symbol gets the operation's summary and description as docs.
- Requests that meet it take payload and reply from it when their block says nothing; the evidence is the description ("from openapi.yaml").
- A declared meet never counts as a second server (no ambiguity warning).
- Operations nobody serves become endpoint nodes inside the description's node (kind api).
- Placement of the description node: [[import.api]] part_of, else x-docair-part-of in the file, else a declared service whose id is slug(info.title), else the package or service that owns the description's directory, else the system. It is removed when nothing is left in it.
- Inside an external part, endpoints nothing requests are dropped.
- Viewer: a glyph for kind api; in the details "Described in openapi.yaml:12 · createOrder · CreateOrder → Order".
acceptance_criteria: On the fixture: create_order and get_order carry their operations; cancelOrder is an endpoint inside the description's node; the cart's line reads (CreateOrder) → Order, from openapi.yaml; only the called payments operation is on the chart; nothing appears twice. Rust tests for placement and matching; an e2e spec checks the page.

No Node or Edge field added: what a description says is in tags and docs. Fixture: the cart calls POST /v1/charges. Golden apis updated; test declared_routes_meet_their_handlers. title: Infra: from a Service to the program its pods run (image, Dockerfile, crate or app)

title: Layout worker: check Firefox and Safari, and test stopping a layout on a large picture in e2e
description:
The layout worker (docair-c5a, @id docair-viewer.layout-worker) has only been checked in Chromium: from file://, over HTTP, and in the web app's sandboxed srcdoc frame. Firefox and Safari are not installed in the devcontainer. Things to check there: a Blob worker made by an opaque-origin document (the web app's frame), and OffscreenCanvas text measurement that matches the page's (otherwise the picture differs). Where the worker does not start, the viewer lays out on the page as before (workerFailed), so nothing breaks, but the page freezes again on large pictures.

The e2e fixtures are too small to test the two things that matter on large pictures: that a click on another layer stops a running layout, and that no frame waits longer than 100 ms. They were measured by script on docair's own page (frame gaps of 20 ms during a 23 s Code layout, Apps drawn 0.78 s after the click).
acceptance_criteria: The page lays out in the worker in Firefox and Safari, from file:// and in the web app, with the same picture as on the page. An e2e fixture, or a generated large graph, lets a test stop a running layout with a layer click and check the frame gaps.

The infra adapter reads Ingress -> Service -> Deployment but not the entry: kind_cluster's extra_port_mappings (host_port -> container_port) in Terraform, the ingress controller's Service (NodePort) in its Helm values, and which controller takes the Ingress (ingressClassName is read).

description: items_by_row keeps only the outermost item per line, so in 'impl Adapter for A { fn file(&self) {} }' or 'mod config { pub fn load() {} }' on one line the inner fn has no symbol: no node, no calls to or from it, and an index definition on that line maps to the impl. title: Apps layer: nginx is drawn as one of docair's programs
description:
On docair's own page, the Apps layer draws nginx as a program, next to docair-cli, docair-server, docair-web and the viewer page. But nginx is off-the-shelf software. In docair it only serves docair-web's built files, inside the docair-web container (docker/web.Dockerfile, docker/nginx.conf). The repository holds its config, not its code.

Why: the doc block in docker/nginx.conf declares `@id nginx`, `@kind service`, `@part-of container.docair-web`. SPEC §3.4 says a program is a `service` or `job` that is not inside another program and not declared in Terraform. The viewer follows that rule (crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js: classify marks every such node `program`; appPart puts every program on Apps). So by the current rule, nginx is a program.

Compare Traefik, also off-the-shelf: it is declared as a `gateway` (k8s.traefik, infra/terraform/ingress.tf), and the Apps layer leaves gateways out.

Two walks pass nginx: `open` (step 7) and `provision` (step 11). Whatever changes, they must still show it.
design:
Options:

| Option | What changes | Effect |
|--------|--------------|--------|
| Declare nginx as a `gateway`, or another kind that Apps leaves out | the doc block in docker/nginx.conf | nginx shows on Network; Apps shows docair's own programs |
| A program needs its code in the repository (a manifest such as Cargo.toml or package.json); a service declared only by a server's config file is not one | SPEC §3.4, classify in viewer.js | every project with an nginx, Redis or Traefik config gets the same |
| Keep it as it is; SPEC says why a server like nginx is a program | SPEC §3.4 | none on the page |
acceptance_criteria: The choice is made and written down (in SPEC §3.4, or in the doc block). docair's own Apps layer shows what it says. The walks open and provision still show nginx at their steps. docair check . stays at 0 errors and 0 warnings.
notes:
Built 2026-11-18, option 1:
- docker/nginx.conf: @kind gateway (was service). The block now says why: nginx is off-the-shelf, like Traefik.
- docs/SPEC.md, kinds table: `gateway` also covers software the project only configures, such as a web server (nginx).

On docair's own page:
| Layer | nginx |
|---|---|
| Apps | left out; the programs are docair-cli, docair-server, docair-viewer.page, terraform, docair-web |
| Network | drawn as itself (before: its Deployment stood for it) |
| Kubernetes | drawn as itself, as before |
| Infrastructure | inside the namespace box, as before |
| Code | left out |

- Apps loses the lines browser → nginx (GET /) and nginx → docair-web (the bundle). The request still bridges to docair-web, but docair-web sits inside the browser box, so no line is drawn. The way in still shows at Network and in the open walk.
- Walks: open plays at Network, and step 7 shows nginx itself (before: its Deployment box). provision plays at Infrastructure; its step 11 sits in step 8 "Inside namespace docair", with nginx in the namespace box, as before.
- The line nginx → docair-web.main carries data.page, and Code now leaves nginx out. The viewer session (data walks) knows.

Validation: docair check . has 0 errors and 0 warnings; e2e 53/53 passed.
close_reason: nginx is now a gateway (docker/nginx.conf), as Traefik is, so the Apps layer shows only docair's own programs. It is drawn as itself on Network and Kubernetes, the walks open and provision still show it, the SPEC kinds table says why, and docair check . is at 0 errors and 0 warnings.

Facts: what adapters learn from the code', which would define *facts* by itself (MEANINGS.md §2) without a decision. title: Following data: say what the walk covers, keep its lines lit, mark data in step titles
description:
When a data walk is short or shows only some of the lines that carry the datum, nothing says so: the card says 'Step 1 of 1', Play and Next do nothing, and it looks as if nothing happened. The lines that carry the datum are not lit while the walk plays (SPEC §3.6 says they stay lit). Step titles name the maker and the datum the same way ('ask.digest makes digest'), which reads like a typo when they share a name.
How to tackle: in the walk's card, say how many lines carry the datum and how many the walk shows, and list the others (for example 'carried by 16 lines; 4 are in this walk, 12 more below'); keep the carrying lines lit during the walk; mark the datum with ◇ in step titles ('ask.digest makes ◇ digest'). Smaller once the reply fix (docair-nkm) lands, since walks then reach more lines.
acceptance_criteria: A data walk that cannot show every carrying line says so in its card and lists the rest; the carrying lines drawn on the layer stay lit while the walk plays; step titles mark data with ◇.
notes: Built (viewer, crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js + viewer.css): (1) The walk card's first step says what the walk covers. carriedLines (@id docair-viewer.data-cover) writes 'Carried by N lines, all in this walk; K of them start stretches of their own, not reached from where it is made.'; it lists lines not in the walk, if any, and the lines this layer does not draw (at most 8, then '… N more'; ends named with nameOf). (2) Lit lines: the carrying lines stay teal (--data, 3.5 px, opacity 1) while the walk plays. applyFollow no longer fades the walk's own parts and lines: the maker, and the lines it travels inside, used to get carry-dim (opacity 0.18). Selected parts are never carry-dimmed (.carry-dim:unselected). (3) The walk's words mark the datum with ◇: 'ask.digest makes ◇ digest', 'brings ◇ reply back', 'Not reached from where ◇ X is made'. Data chips no longer match the end of a dotted part name ('ask.digest'). On docair's page: digest 'Carried by 1 line, in this walk.'; reply 'Carried by 23 lines, all in this walk; 4 of them start stretches of their own…'; at Apps reply lists 17 lines not drawn. Tests: e2e/tests/data.spec.ts checks the card line, ◇ titles, lit lines and no carry-dim on the walk's parts (shop and answer fixtures). e2e 53/53; docair check 0 errors, 0 warnings. SPEC §3.6.
close_reason: Data walk cards say what the walk covers and list what the layer does not draw; carrying lines stay lit and the walk's parts never fade; the walk's words mark data with ◇.

title: Viewer: the data kind has no colours (console warnings, empty legend swatch)
description: The viewer's style gives every entry of KINDS a fill and an outline from viewer.css (crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js, makeStyle: --k-<kind>-bg and --k-<kind>-line), but viewer.css has no --k-data-bg or --k-data-line. So every page logs two Cytoscape warnings when it loads ('The style property `background-color: ` is invalid', and the same for border-color), and the legend's '◇ data' entry shows an empty swatch (transparent fill). Data parts are never drawn on the canvas (they have their own list, SPEC §3.6), so nothing else shows it. Seen on docair's own page and on the e2e fixture pages. Fix: define the two colours for data in viewer.css (light and dark), or leave data out of the canvas style and colour its legend swatch directly.
acceptance_criteria: A page loads with no console warnings; the legend's data entry shows a coloured swatch in light and dark mode.
